newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Westpactrust cuts NZ variable mortgage rate.
newsitem.headline: Westpactrust cuts NZ variable mortgage rate.

text.p: Westpactrust Bank said on Friday it had cut its variable home lending rate to 8.95 percent from 9.4 percent.

WestpacTrust chief executive Harry Price said the new rate, effective immediately for new customers and from August 14 for new borrowers, had been made possible by the Reserve Bank's endorsement on Friday of recent lower wholesale interest rates.
"It is now appropriate for us to pass these lower rates onto our customers," Price said in a statement.
Rates on 90-day bank bills, an important source of mortgage funding, slipped sharply on the Reserve Bank's statement, to close at 6.92 percent from 7.01 percent yesterday.
Guardian Trust also reduced its one year fixed residential mortgage rate to 7.95 percent, from 8.50 percent, following today's Reserve Bank monetary policy statement.

Mortgage manager William Cairns said the statement effectively sanctioned lower interest rates built into the wholesale market recently, and Guardian took a positive view on the future for mortgage rates. The new fixed rate is effective today.
Cairns said Guardian's variable rate remained at 8.50 percent, but he expected variable rates generally to come under downward pressure over the next three to four weeks.
There was little inflationary pressure and with a slow economy demand for money was down, he said.
He thought rates on 90-day bills could fall to around 6.70 percent over the next month.
